subject: Novus Health: AZ3 latency spiral & traffic diversion
messages:
From: ops@novushealth.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spiral in us-west-az3 — urgent

Kimberly / Rishi,

We are seeing a rapid degradation in production starting ~08:00 PDT in our us-west (AZ3) region. Key symptoms: p95 latency jumped from ~380ms to 3.2s, request error rate up to 6% (5xx and model OOMs), and effective throughput has dropped ~40% despite steady incoming traffic. Token- and request-level traces point to repeated KV cache churn and worker restarts.

This is impacting our critical billing and ingestion pipelines — customers are seeing timeouts. Our ops team is requesting an immediate cross-region diversion to eastus2 and an explanation of risk (cache invalidation, session affinity loss). Please advise next steps and ETA for mitigations.

Attaching a short trace bundle and a sample error dump.

— Elaine Choi
Site Reliability Lead, Novus Health
attachments: novus_latency_log_090307.zip
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ops@novushealth.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:18:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spiral in us-west-az3 — urgent

Elaine —

Thanks for the rapid flag. We're treating this as P0. Rishi and I are pulling infra and runtime leads into the war room now. Immediate plan: 1) runbook activation and traffic diversion canary -> 10% in 10m; 2) enable degraded model variant (quantized) for low-latency paths; 3) request one-time SLA exception/credit conversation with our partnerships/sales team.

Marissa — please start the diversion canary and post step-by-step in this thread with timestamps. Rishi/Sean, please prepare the exec summary and proposed credit ask for Novus. Elaine — we'll comment here as we make changes; please share any additional traces.

I'll maintain the customer-facing comms.

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
redwood.com
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:25:10 -0700
Subject: RE: Production latency spiral in us-west-az3 — urgent

All — quick technical proposal:
- Traffic steering: route 60% of Novus production traffic from us-west-az3 -> eastus2 via smart-router override. Start with 10% canary for 10 minutes, then 30%, then 60%.
- Runtime change: deploy quantized model variant (reduced memory footprint) to eastus2 to avoid K/V-cache warmup penalties. This will reduce per-token quality slightly — flag to Novus as degraded-mode.
- Cache behavior: expect ~15–25% request retries during warmup; advise session-affinity loss for websocket connections.
- Cloud partner: opening an Azure support ticket for underlying host restarts and to confirm capacity in eastus2.

Sean — customer asks for credits. I propose offering a two-week credit of committed capacity and an expedited RCA with a follow-on architectural review. If legal needs decision, I can escalate.

I'll coordinate the router override. Marissa — can you confirm routing controls and expected invalidation window?

Rishi
Director, Customer Solutions
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: ops@novushealth.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:35:55 -0700
Subject: RE: Production latency spiral in us-west-az3 — urgent

Activated the routing override at 08:35. Steps executed:
1) Canary 10% -> monitoring (08:35–08:45): initial errors reduced, p95 to ~900ms for canary path.
2) Ramp to 30% at 08:50 after green canary. Observed cache-miss spike; issued cache prewarm job.
3) Ramp to 60% at 09:20. Eastus2 served ~58% traffic by 09:25.

Notes/risks: session-based websocket sessions will not stick to eastus2 automatically — some reconnections required. We invalidated a small subset of KV entries to avoid corrupt state; expected warmup window ~18–35 minutes. Attached deployment snapshot (deployment-snapshot-az3.json) and a short log excerpt.

We have also engaged Azure support (ticket #AZ-71291).

— Marissa Cole
Senior Infra Ops, Redwood Inference
attachments: deployment-snapshot-az3.json
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: ops@novushealth.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:45:03 -0700
Subject: Novus — immediate remediation & next steps

Elaine / Novus team —

Thanks for bearing with us. Kimberly and the infra team implemented a cross-region diversion to eastus2 and we believe the majority of customer requests are now being served from the alternate region. I’m sorry for the disruption — we know this impacts revenue-critical flows.

We are offering two weeks of committed-capacity credit as a one-time gesture while we complete the RCA. We will also commit to a prioritized architectural review within 10 business days to discuss double-writing sessions and affinity improvements. Can you confirm acceptance of the proposed credit and timing for the review?

Kimberly will follow up with the full incident timeline and post-mortem.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: ops@novushealth.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novus — immediate remediation & next steps

Kimberly / Sean / Marissa —

Thanks for the rapid response and the diversion. Eastus2 is handling traffic but we continue to see intermittent 5xx spikes (~0.5–1%) for specific ingestion endpoints; those appear tied to a small subset of batched requests that lose KV-context during retries. We'll hold on acceptance of credits pending the RCA, but appreciate the offer.

Please include the timeline of the routing steps, exact TTLs for cache invalidation, and the Azure ticket updates in the post-incident report. We also request a short follow-up call tomorrow at 09:00 PT to review mitigation and next steps.
